## Overview

When you search for an **eToro review 2026 is it safe**, you’re likely weighing the platform’s reputation against the ever‑changing landscape of online trading. eToro has been around since 2007, evolving from a simple forex broker into a multi‑asset hub that blends traditional investing with social trading. By 2026, the platform boasts millions of users across more than 140 countries, offering stocks, ETFs, commodities, indices, and a growing selection of cryptocurrencies. Its hallmark feature—CopyTrader—lets you automatically mirror the trades of top‑performing investors, which appeals to newcomers who want to learn by doing while still maintaining control over their capital.

The question of safety is paramount. In this review we’ll dig into the regulatory framework that governs eToro, examine how client funds are protected, and weigh the platform’s strengths against any potential drawbacks. Whether you’re a beginner testing the waters or a seasoned trader looking for a social edge, understanding the safety nets in place will help you decide if eToro fits your 2026 trading goals.

## Safety & Regulation

### Licenses and Oversight

eToro operates under several reputable licenses that vary by region. In Europe, it is regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) under license number 109/10. For UK clients, eToro (UK) Ltd holds authorization from the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) under reference number 583263. Australian users are covered by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) license 491139. These regulators impose strict capital adequacy rules, regular audits, and transparent reporting requirements, which collectively aim to safeguard investor interests.

### Fund Protection

Client money segregation is a cornerstone of eToro’s safety model. Funds deposited by users are kept in separate bank accounts distinct from the company’s operational capital. In the EU, this segregation is backed by the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF), which can compensate eligible clients up to €20,000 if the broker becomes insolvent. In the UK, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) offers protection up to £85,000 per person. Australia’s ASIC framework provides similar safeguards through the Financial Claims Scheme (FCS). While no platform can guarantee absolute safety, these layers of protection significantly reduce the risk of loss due to broker misconduct.

## Key Features

### Social Trading

The social trading network remains eToro’s biggest draw. You can browse trader profiles, view their historical performance, risk scores, and portfolio composition. The CopyTrader tool lets you allocate a portion of your balance to automatically replicate a chosen trader’s moves in real time. You retain the ability to stop copying at any moment, adjust allocation percentages, or set stop‑loss limits on copied trades.

### CopyPortfolios

For those who prefer a more hands‑off approach, CopyPortfolios are thematic baskets managed by eToro’s investment committee or top traders. Examples include “InTheMoney” (dividend‑focused stocks), “CryptoPortfolio” (a curated mix of digital assets), and “Gaming” (stocks tied to the video‑game industry). These portfolios rebalance periodically, offering diversification without the need to pick individual assets.

### Crypto Offering

By 2026, eToro has expanded its crypto roster to over 70 coins, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and newer DeFi tokens. Users can buy, sell, and hold cryptocurrencies directly on the platform, or use them as underlying assets for CopyTrader strategies. The platform also provides a crypto wallet for transferring assets to external addresses, though withdrawals may incur network fees and are subject to KYC verification.
